articles.summary: Humans have been on this planet for a blink in geological time. Perhaps you’ve heard the analogy that if the 4.5 billion-year history of the Earth was compressed into 24 hours, all of recorded human history would last but a few seconds before midnight. I’m writing to tell you why this is not the full story. By understanding more of the 23 hours and 58 minutes before our species arrived, we can comprehend why this moment in time is not just another instant; it’s a critical point of evolution, not only for our species but for the biosphere as a whole.
articles.title: Why Paleobiology Is Critical to our Climate Future

articles.summary: Earth in the Archean Eon, 4,000 to 2,500 million years ago, appeared as an alien world. The planet’s crust was stabilizing, green oceans were filled with dissolved iron, and the atmosphere had negligible oxygen. Microbial life subsisted on chemical energy extracted from boiling plumes erupting miles deep in dark, hydrothermal vents, as it already had done for over a billion years.
